reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC2131-2-3.note: Server clause enforced: TestFlagsReservedBitsIgnored sends flags 0x7fff and asserts the reply still unicasts to yiaddr:68 as for flags 0. Client clause proven for acquisition only: TestRFC2131ClientSetsReservedFlagsBitsToZero (guest, real client over veth) reads the DISCOVER (positive) and, after an OFFER with flags 0xffff, the REQUEST (negative); a no-op of clearReservedFlags reddens the negative (REQUEST flags 0xffff), while the recorded break is a panic revert that reddens both before their assertions, and the positive stays green under a no-op because nclient4 builds the DISCOVER with flags 0. Missing: the renewal path. vendored NewRenewFromAck copies the ACK's flags (WithReply, then only WithBroadcast(false)), and renewV4 fixes that by passing clearReservedFlags to client.Renew; no test drives a renewal, so dropping that argument stays green (question 4, a second producer path)

RFC2131-3-1.note: positive reads octets 236..239 of OFFER, ACK and NAK and pins 0x63825363; negative replaces the cookie with 0xDEADBEEF and asserts h.handle returns nil

RFC2131-3.2-4.note: positive relays a SELECTING REQUEST with giaddr 192.168.1.254 and asserts responseAddr gives 192.168.1.254:67 for the resulting NAK; negative asserts the same NAK with giaddr zero goes to 255.255.255.255:68, not to a relay

RFC2131-4.1-15.note: gap confirmed at the producer: no reader interprets option overload (52), and every reader walks pkt[240:] only, so an option a client places in file or sname is never read; row quote is the verbatim section 4.1 sentence 4.1-7 dropped

RFC2131-4.1-3.note: positive walks each OFFER/ACK/NAK option by its length octets and requires reaching End (255); negative fills a request's options with 0x01 so it carries no End, and requires the reply to be End-terminated

RFC2131-4.1-6.note: positive: TestRFC2131EveryReplyOptionContainedInItsField walks OFFER, ACK and the separately built DHCPNAK by length octets to End inside the options field and requires sname/file all zero with no option 52; TestOptionsContainedWithinTheirField keeps the OFFER/ACK walk. negative: a 300-octet bootfile; judge overlay removing the 255 guard in safeAppendOption reddens it ('option code 98 at offset 555 declares length 98, overrunning the options field'). Receiver side: TestOptionsContainedWithinTheirField negative, an overrunning received option is not read past the field. Config refuses bootfile-bios/uefi over 255 (TestParsePXEConfigInvalid)

RFC2131-4.1-7.note: gap confirmed at the producer: every server option reader walks pkt[240:], the options field alone, and nothing reads option 52; the server fills the receiver role, so not-applicable was wrong and the gap is honest

RFC2131-4.2-2.note: positive: same chaddr, different xid and flags, no option 61, draws the same address (TestRFC2131ChaddrContentsIdentifyTheClient; TestChaddrIdentifiesClientWithoutClientIdentifier positive kept). negative: same xid, chaddr differing in first or last octet only, draws a different address, so identity keyed on xid or on part of chaddr goes red. The old hlen=0 negative tag is correctly removed: the RFC says nothing about a zero-length chaddr

RFC2131-4.3-1.note: single-polarity positive: option 54 in OFFER, ACK and NAK must equal the server address, so omitting or mis-setting it goes red

RFC2131-4.3-2.note: single-polarity positive: the OFFER's option 51 must be four octets equal to the configured lease seconds

RFC2131-4.3-3.note: single-polarity positive: the ACK answering a DHCPREQUEST must carry option 51 equal to the configured lease seconds

RFC2131-4.3-4.note: positive: the NAK's option walk holds no 51; negative: a REQUEST carrying option 51 that is NAKed still yields a NAK without 51

RFC2131-4.3-5.note: positive: no OFFER/ACK/NAK carries option 50; negative: requests carrying option 50 still draw OFFER/ACK/NAK without it

RFC2131-4.3-6.note: positive: neither OFFER nor ACK carries option 61; negative: requests carrying option 61 still draw OFFER/ACK without it. The NAK column (MAY) is correctly left unasserted

RFC2131-4.3-7.note: positive: no OFFER/ACK/NAK carries option 55; negative: requests carrying option 55 still draw replies without it

RFC2131-4.3-8.note: positive: no OFFER/ACK/NAK carries option 57; negative: requests carrying option 57 still draw replies without it

RFC2131-4.3-9.note: positive and negative both require every NAK option code to be 53 or 54, so any option Table 3 marks 'All others' goes red. The assertion is stricter than Table 3: it would also go red on the Message option (56, SHOULD), Client identifier (61, MAY) and Vendor class identifier (60, MAY), which Table 3 allows in a DHCPNAK

RFC2131-4.3.1-2.note: positive: requested subnet mask, router, DNS and domain name each equal the configured bytes exactly (DNS now byte for byte, closing the length-only gap); negative: a request suggesting other values for all four still gets the configured ones, so a server echoing client-suggested values goes red. {single-polarity} correctly removed from the row

RFC2131-4.3.1-4.note: Forbidden: returning a value for a parameter the server has no value for (neither configured nor a Host Requirements default). TestUnconfiguredParametersOmitted builds a handler with no router, DNS or domain name configured; the negative tag sends a DISCOVER whose parameter request list explicitly names optRouter, optDNS and optDomainName and asserts askedCodes[code] is false for each, so any emitted option for them (including an empty or zero-valued one, since replyOptionCodes records presence by code) goes red. The positive tag asserts the same absence for an unrequested DISCOVER. None of the three has a Host Requirements default, so the ELSE branch applies.

RFC2131-4.3.1-6.note: Forbidden: a requested parameter included more than once in a reply (no option ze emits is one the options document allows to repeat). TestEachParameterEmittedOnce counts every option code in the OFFER and ACK with replyOptionCounts and fails on n != 1 (positive); the negative tag sends a DISCOVER whose parameter request list repeats router, DNS and subnet mask, carries a second PRL and an echoed router option, to both a plain and a PXE server, and fails on any option count other than 1, so a duplicated parameter goes red.

RFC2131-4.4.5-3.note: positive: for leases 60, 3600, 86400 and 604800 the OFFER's option 59 (T2) must be strictly below the lease seconds; negative: parseConfig must reject lease-time 0
